part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: PART IV HOW PERSEUS CAME TO THE ÆTHIOPS

translation.en: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Aethiops
translation.kr: 제4부: 페르세우스가 에티오피아에 이르다

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: So Perseus flitted onward to the north-east, over many a league of sea, till he came to the rolling sand-hills and the dreary Lybian shore.

translation.en: Perseus flew onward to the northeast over many leagues of sea.
translation.kr: 페르세우스는 끝없는 바다를 지나 북동쪽으로 날아갔습니다.

translation.en: Finally, he reached the rolling sand hills and the dreary Libyan shore.
translation.kr: 마침내 그는 굽이치는 모래 언덕과 황량한 리비아 해안에 이르렀습니다.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: And he flitted on across the desert: over rock-ledges, and banks of shingle, and level wastes of sand, and shell-drifts bleaching in the sunshine, and the skeletons of great sea-monsters, and dead bones of ancient giants, strewn up and down upon the old sea-floor.  And as he went the blood-drops fell to the earth from the Gorgon’s head, and became poisonous asps and adders, which breed in the desert to this day.

translation.en: He flew on across the desert over rocky ledges and banks of pebbles.
translation.kr: 그는 암석 지대와 자갈밭을 넘어 사막을 가로질러 날아갔습니다.

translation.en: He passed level wastes of sand and piles of shells bleaching in the sunshine.
translation.kr: 그는 평평한 모래 황무지와 햇빛에 바랜 조개껍데기 더미를 지나쳤습니다.

translation.en: The skeletons of great sea monsters and dead bones of ancient giants were strewn across the old sea floor.
translation.kr: 거대한 바다 괴물의 골격과 고대 거인들의 마른 뼈가 오래된 해저 곳곳에 흩어져 있었습니다.

translation.en: As he traveled, blood fell to the earth from the Gorgon head.
translation.kr: 그가 이동하는 동안 고르곤의 머리에서 핏방울이 땅으로 떨어졌습니다.

translation.en: These drops became the poisonous snakes that breed in the desert to this day.
translation.kr: 이 핏방울들은 오늘날까지도 사막에 서식하는 맹독성 뱀이 되었습니다.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: Over the sands he went,—he never knew how far or how long, feeding on the fruit which the Nymphs had given him, till he saw the hills of the Psylli, and the Dwarfs who fought with cranes.  Their spears were of reeds and rushes, and their houses of the egg-shells of the cranes; and Perseus laughed, and went his way to the north-east, hoping all day long to see the blue Mediterranean sparkling, that he might fly across it to his home.

translation.en: He traveled over the sands for an unknown distance and time.
translation.kr: 그는 모래 위를 얼마나 멀리, 얼마나 오랫동안 갔는지 모른 채 여행했습니다.

translation.en: He survived by eating the fruit the nymphs had given him.
translation.kr: 그는 요정들이 준 과일을 먹으며 버텼습니다.

translation.en: Eventually, he saw the hills of the Psylli and the Dwarfs who fought with cranes.
translation.kr: 마침내 그는 프실리 언덕과 두루미들과 싸우는 난쟁이들을 보았습니다.

translation.en: Their spears were made of reeds, and their houses were built from crane eggshells.
translation.kr: 그들의 창은 갈대로 만들어졌고, 집은 두루미의 알껍데기로 지어졌습니다.

translation.en: Perseus laughed and continued his way to the northeast.
translation.kr: 페르세우스는 웃음을 터뜨리며 북동쪽으로 길을 재촉했습니다.

translation.en: He hoped to see the sparkling blue Mediterranean so he could fly home.
translation.kr: 그는 푸른 지중해가 반짝이는 모습을 보고 무사히 고향으로 날아가기를 온종일 바랐습니다.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: But now came down a mighty wind, and swept him back southward toward the desert.  All day long he strove against it; but even the winged sandals could not prevail.  So he was forced to float down the wind all night; and when the morning dawned there was nothing to be seen, save the same old hateful waste of sand.

translation.en: Suddenly, a mighty wind swept him back southward toward the desert.
translation.kr: 갑자기 강력한 바람이 불어와 그를 사막이 있는 남쪽으로 휩쓸어 갔습니다.

translation.en: He struggled against it all day, but even his winged sandals could not overcome the gale.
translation.kr: 그는 온종일 바람과 맞서 싸웠지만, 날개 달린 샌들조차 폭풍을 이겨낼 수 없었습니다.

translation.en: He was forced to float with the wind all night.
translation.kr: 그는 밤새도록 바람에 떠밀려갈 수밖에 없었습니다.

translation.en: When morning dawned, nothing was visible except the same hateful waste of sand.
translation.kr: 아침이 밝았을 때, 지긋지긋한 모래 황무지 외에는 아무것도 보이지 않았습니다.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: And out of the north the sandstorms rushed upon him, blood-red pillars and wreaths, blotting out the noonday sun; and Perseus fled before them, lest he should be choked by the burning dust.  At last the gale fell calm, and he tried to go northward again; but again came down the sandstorms, and swept him back into the waste, and then all was calm and cloudless as before.  Seven days he strove against the storms, and seven days he was driven back, till he was spent with thirst and hunger, and his tongue clove to the roof of his mouth.  Here and there he fancied that he saw a fair lake, and the sunbeams shining on the water; but when he came to it it vanished at his feet, and there was nought but burning sand.  And if he had not been of the race of the Immortals, he would have perished in the waste; but his life was strong within him, because it was more than man’s.

translation.en: Blood-red sandstorms rushed upon him from the north.
translation.kr: 북쪽에서 핏빛 모래폭풍이 그를 덮쳤습니다.

translation.en: They blotted out the noonday sun, and Perseus fled before them to avoid suffocating.
translation.kr: 폭풍이 한낮의 태양을 가려버렸고, 페르세우스는 숨이 막히지 않으려고 도망쳤습니다.

translation.en: When the gale finally calmed, he tried to head north again.
translation.kr: 마침내 강풍이 잦아들자 그는 다시 북쪽으로 향하려 했습니다.

translation.en: But the sandstorms returned and swept him back into the wasteland.
translation.kr: 하지만 모래폭풍이 다시 돌아와 그를 황무지로 휩쓸어 갔습니다.

translation.en: He fought the storms for seven days and was driven back for seven days.
translation.kr: 그는 칠 일 동안 폭풍과 싸웠고, 칠 일 동안 뒤로 밀려났습니다.

translation.en: He was completely exhausted by thirst and hunger.
translation.kr: 그는 갈증과 굶주림으로 완전히 지쳐버렸습니다.

translation.en: His tongue stuck to the roof of his mouth.
translation.kr: 그의 혀는 입천장에 달라붙었습니다.

translation.en: Occasionally, he imagined seeing a beautiful lake sparkling in the sun.
translation.kr: 때때로 그는 햇빛에 반짝이는 아름다운 호수를 본다고 착각했습니다.

translation.en: But when he approached, it vanished into burning sand.
translation.kr: 하지만 그가 다가가면 호수는 불타는 모래 속으로 사라졌습니다.

translation.en: If he had not been immortal, he would have died in the wasteland.
translation.kr: 그가 불멸의 존재가 아니었다면 황무지에서 목숨을 잃었을 것입니다.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: Then he cried to Athené, and said—

translation.en: Then he cried out to Athena and said:
translation.kr: 그때 그는 아테나를 부르며 외쳤습니다.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: ‘Oh, fair and pure, if thou hearest me, wilt thou leave me here to die of drought?  I have brought thee the Gorgon’s head at thy bidding, and hitherto thou hast prospered my journey; dost thou desert me at the last? Else why will not these immortal sandals prevail, even against the desert storms?  Shall I never see my mother more, and the blue ripple round Seriphos, and the sunny hills of Hellas?’

translation.en: Oh fair and pure goddess, will you leave me here to die of thirst?
translation.kr: 오 아름답고 순결하신 여신이여, 저를 이곳에 버려두어 목말라 죽게 하시렵니까?

translation.en: I brought you the Gorgon head as you commanded.
translation.kr: 저는 당신의 명령대로 고르곤의 머리를 가져왔습니다.

translation.en: You have blessed my journey so far; will you desert me at the end?
translation.kr: 지금까지 제 여행을 축복해주셨으면서, 마지막에 저를 버리시나이까?

translation.en: Why else would these immortal sandals fail against the desert storms?
translation.kr: 그렇지 않다면 어찌하여 이 불멸의 샌들이 사막의 폭풍을 이겨내지 못한단 말입니까?

translation.en: Will I never see my mother, the blue waves of Seriphos, or the sunny hills of Greece again?
translation.kr: 어머니와 세리포스의 푸른 물결, 그리고 그리스의 햇살 가득한 언덕을 다시는 볼 수 없는 것입니까?

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: So he prayed; and after he had prayed there was a great silence.

translation.en: He prayed, and after his prayer, a great silence fell.
translation.kr: 그는 그렇게 기도했고, 기도가 끝난 후 깊은 침묵이 흘렀습니다.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: The heaven was still above his head, and the sand was still beneath his feet; and Perseus looked up, but there was nothing but the blinding sun in the blinding blue; and round him, but there was nothing but the blinding sand.

translation.en: The sky was still above his head, and the sand was still beneath his feet.
translation.kr: 하늘은 여전히 그의 머리 위에 있었고, 모래는 여전히 발밑에 있었습니다.

translation.en: Perseus looked up, but saw nothing but the blinding sun in the blue sky.
translation.kr: 페르세우스가 위를 올려다보았지만, 눈부신 푸른 하늘의 태양 외에는 아무것도 없었습니다.

translation.en: Around him, there was nothing but the blinding sand.
translation.kr: 그의 주위에는 눈부신 모래뿐이었습니다.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: And Perseus stood still a while, and waited, and said, ‘Surely I am not here without the will of the Immortals, for Athené will not lie.  Were not these sandals to lead me in the right road?  Then the road in which I have tried to go must be a wrong road.’

translation.en: Perseus stood still for a while and waited.
translation.kr: 페르세우스는 잠시 가만히 서서 기다렸습니다.

translation.en: I am surely not here without the gods will, for Athena does not lie, he said.
translation.kr: 아테나 여신은 거짓말을 하지 않으시니, 내가 신들의 뜻 없이 이곳에 있는 것은 아닐 것이다, 그가 말했습니다.

translation.en: Were these sandals not meant to lead me on the right path?
translation.kr: 이 샌들은 나를 올바른 길로 이끌어주기로 되어 있지 않았던가?

translation.en: Then the road I have been trying to take must be the wrong one.
translation.kr: 그렇다면 내가 가려고 했던 길은 분명 잘못된 길일 것이다.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: Then suddenly his ears were opened, and he heard the sound of running water.

translation.en: Suddenly, his ears were opened, and he heard the sound of running water.
translation.kr: 갑자기 그의 귀가 열리며 흐르는 물소리가 들렸습니다.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: And at that his heart was lifted up, though he scarcely dare believe his ears; and weary as he was, he hurried forward, though he could scarcely stand upright; and within a bowshot of him was a glen in the sand, and marble rocks, and date-trees, and a lawn of gay green grass.  And through the lawn a streamlet sparkled and wandered out beyond the trees, and vanished in the sand.

translation.en: His heart lifted, though he could scarcely believe his ears.
translation.kr: 그는 자신의 귀를 의심했지만 가슴이 벅차올랐습니다.

translation.en: As weary as he was, he hurried forward, barely able to stand upright.
translation.kr: 그는 똑바로 서 있기조차 힘들 만큼 지쳐 있었지만 서둘러 앞으로 나아갔습니다.

translation.en: Within a bowshot was a glen in the sand with marble rocks and date trees.
translation.kr: 활이 닿을 거리에 대리석 바위와 대추야자 나무가 있는 모래 계곡이 있었습니다.

translation.en: A stream sparkled through a lawn of bright green grass.
translation.kr: 밝고 푸른 잔디밭 위로 시냇물이 반짝이며 흐르고 있었습니다.

translation.en: It wandered out beyond the trees and vanished into the sand.
translation.kr: 시냇물은 나무 밖으로 구불구불 흘러나가 모래 속으로 사라졌습니다.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: The water trickled among the rocks, and a pleasant breeze rustled in the dry date-branches and Perseus laughed for joy, and leapt down the cliff, and drank of the cool water, and ate of the dates, and slept upon the turf, and leapt up and went forward again: but not toward the north this time; for he said, ‘Surely Athené hath sent me hither, and will not have me go homeward yet.  What if there be another noble deed to be done, before I see the sunny hills of Hellas?’

translation.en: The water trickled among the rocks, and a pleasant breeze rustled the dry date branches.
translation.kr: 물은 바위 사이로 졸졸 흘렀고, 기분 좋은 산들바람이 마른 대추야자 가지를 스쳤습니다.

translation.en: Perseus laughed for joy and leaped down the cliff to drink the cool water.
translation.kr: 페르세우스는 기뻐하며 웃었고, 절벽 아래로 뛰어내려 시원한 물을 마셨습니다.

translation.en: He ate the dates, slept upon the turf, and woke up ready to move forward.
translation.kr: 그는 대추야자를 먹고 잔디 위에서 잠을 잔 뒤, 다시 앞으로 나아갈 준비를 마치고 일어났습니다.

translation.en: This time he did not go north.
translation.kr: 이번에는 북쪽으로 가지 않았습니다.

translation.en: Surely Athena has sent me here and does not want me to go home yet, he said.
translation.kr: 분명 아테나 여신께서 나를 이곳으로 보내셨고, 아직 고향에 가기를 원치 않으시는구나, 그가 말했습니다.

translation.en: What if there is another noble deed to be done before I see Greece again?
translation.kr: 내가 다시 그리스를 보기 전에 해야 할 고귀한 일이 남아있는 것이라면?

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: So he went east, and east for ever, by fresh oases and fountains, date-palms, and lawns of grass, till he saw before him a mighty mountain-wall, all rose-red in the setting sun.

translation.en: So he traveled constantly eastward by fresh oases, fountains, and date palms.
translation.kr: 그래서 그는 신선한 오아시스와 샘물, 대추야자 나무를 따라 계속해서 동쪽으로 여행했습니다.

translation.en: Finally, he saw a mighty mountain wall glowing rose-red in the setting sun.
translation.kr: 마침내 그는 석양빛을 받아 장미처럼 붉게 빛나는 거대한 산벽을 보았습니다.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: Then he towered in the air like an eagle, for his limbs were strong again; and he flew all night across the mountain till the day began to dawn, and rosy-fingered Eos came blushing up the sky.  And then, behold, beneath him was the long green garden of Egypt and the shining stream of Nile.

translation.en: His strength returned, and he soared into the air like an eagle.
translation.kr: 그는 기운을 되찾고 독수리처럼 하늘 높이 솟아올랐습니다.

translation.en: He flew across the mountain all night until the rosy dawn appeared.
translation.kr: 그는 장밋빛 새벽이 밝아올 때까지 밤새도록 산을 넘어 날아갔습니다.

translation.en: Below him lay the long green gardens of Egypt and the shining Nile river.
translation.kr: 그의 아래로는 이집트의 길고 푸른 정원과 반짝이는 나일강이 펼쳐져 있었습니다.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: And he saw cities walled up to heaven, and temples, and obelisks, and pyramids, and giant Gods of stone.  And he came down amid fields of barley, and flax, and millet, and clambering gourds; and saw the people coming out of the gates of a great city, and setting to work, each in his place, among the water-courses, parting the streams among the plants cunningly with their feet, according to the wisdom of the Egyptians.  But when they saw him they all stopped their work, and gathered round him, and cried—

translation.en: He saw towering cities, temples, obelisks, pyramids, and giant stone gods.
translation.kr: 그는 높이 솟은 도시와 신전, 오벨리스크, 피라미드, 그리고 거대한 돌로 된 신상들을 보았습니다.

translation.en: He landed amid fields of barley, flax, millet, and climbing gourds.
translation.kr: 그는 보리와 아마, 수수, 덩굴 식물이 자라는 들판 한가운데로 내려앉았습니다.

translation.en: The people came out of the city gates to work in the water courses.
translation.kr: 사람들은 수로에서 일하기 위해 성문 밖으로 나왔습니다.

translation.en: They skillfully parted the streams among the plants using their feet.
translation.kr: 그들은 발을 사용해 식물 사이로 능숙하게 물길을 나누었습니다.

translation.en: When they saw him, they stopped working, gathered around, and cried out.
translation.kr: 그들은 그를 보자마자 일손을 멈추고 주위로 몰려들어 외쳤습니다.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: ‘Who art thou, fair youth? and what bearest thou beneath thy goat-skin there?  Surely thou art one of the Immortals; for thy skin is white like ivory, and ours is red like clay.  Thy hair is like threads of gold, and ours is black and curled.  Surely thou art one of the Immortals;’ and they would have worshipped him then and there; but Perseus said—

translation.en: Who are you, fair youth, and what do you carry beneath your goatskin?
translation.kr: 아름다운 청년이여, 당신은 누구시며 그 염소 가죽 아래에 무엇을 가지고 계십니까?

translation.en: Surely you are one of the gods, for your skin is white as ivory.
translation.kr: 당신의 피부는 상아처럼 하야니, 분명 신들 중 한 분이실 겁니다.

translation.en: Our skin is red like clay, and your hair is like threads of gold.
translation.kr: 우리의 피부는 진흙처럼 붉고, 당신의 머리카락은 금실과 같습니다.

translation.en: Surely you are immortal, they said, ready to worship him.
translation.kr: 그들은 분명 당신은 불멸의 존재이십니다, 라고 말하며 그를 숭배하려 했습니다.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: ‘I am not one of the Immortals; but I am a hero of the Hellens.  And I have slain the Gorgon in the wilderness, and bear her head with me.  Give me food, therefore, that I may go forward and finish my work.’

translation.en: I am not immortal; I am a hero of the Greeks, Perseus replied.
translation.kr: 저는 불멸의 존재가 아니라 그리스의 영웅입니다, 페르세우스가 대답했습니다.

translation.en: I have slain the Gorgon in the wilderness and carry her head with me.
translation.kr: 저는 황야에서 고르곤을 죽이고 그 머리를 가지고 왔습니다.

translation.en: Give me food so I may continue my journey and finish my work.
translation.kr: 여행을 계속하고 제 임무를 마칠 수 있도록 음식을 주십시오.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: Then they gave him food, and fruit, and wine; but they would not let him go.  And when the news came into the city that the Gorgon was slain, the priests came out to meet him, and the maidens, with songs and dances, and timbrels and harps; and they would have brought him to their temple and to their king; but Perseus put on the hat of darkness, and vanished away out of their sight.

translation.en: They gave him food, fruit, and wine, but they would not let him go.
translation.kr: 그들은 그에게 음식과 과일, 포도주를 주었지만 그를 보내주려 하지 않았습니다.

translation.en: News reached the city that the Gorgon was slain.
translation.kr: 고르곤이 죽었다는 소식이 도시에 전해졌습니다.

translation.en: Priests and maidens came out to meet him with songs, dances, and harps.
translation.kr: 제사장들과 처녀들이 노래하고 춤추며 수금을 연주하며 그를 맞이하러 나왔습니다.

translation.en: They wanted to bring him to their temple and their king.
translation.kr: 그들은 그를 자신들의 신전과 왕에게 데려가고 싶어 했습니다.

translation.en: But Perseus put on the hat of darkness and vanished from their sight.
translation.kr: 하지만 페르세우스는 어둠의 모자를 쓰고 그들의 시야에서 사라졌습니다.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: Therefore the Egyptians looked long for his return, but in vain, and worshipped him as a hero, and made a statue of him in Chemmis, which stood for many a hundred years; and they said that he appeared to them at times, with sandals a cubit long; and that whenever he appeared the season was fruitful, and the Nile rose high that year.

translation.en: The Egyptians waited long for his return in vain.
translation.kr: 이집트인들은 그가 돌아오기를 오랫동안 기다렸지만 헛수고였습니다.

translation.en: They worshipped him as a hero and made a statue of him in Chemmis.
translation.kr: 그들은 그를 영웅으로 숭배하며 켐미스에 그의 조각상을 세웠습니다.

translation.en: The statue stood for hundreds of years.
translation.kr: 그 조각상은 수백 년 동안 그 자리에 서 있었습니다.

translation.en: They claimed he occasionally appeared to them with enormous sandals.
translation.kr: 그들은 때때로 그가 거대한 샌들을 신고 나타난다고 믿었습니다.

translation.en: Whenever he appeared, the season was fruitful and the Nile rose high.
translation.kr: 그가 나타날 때마다 풍년이 들고 나일강의 수위가 높게 차올랐습니다.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: Then Perseus went to the eastward, along the Red Sea shore; and then, because he was afraid to go into the Arabian deserts, he turned northward once more, and this time no storm hindered him.

translation.en: Perseus traveled eastward along the shore of the Red Sea.
translation.kr: 페르세우스는 홍해 연안을 따라 동쪽으로 이동했습니다.

translation.en: Afraid to enter the Arabian deserts, he turned north once more.
translation.kr: 그는 아라비아 사막으로 들어가는 것이 두려워 다시 북쪽으로 방향을 틀었습니다.

translation.en: This time, no storm hindered his path.
translation.kr: 이번에는 어떤 폭풍도 그의 길을 방해하지 않았습니다.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: He went past the Isthmus, and Mount Casius, and the vast Serbonian bog, and up the shore of Palestine, where the dark-faced Æthiops dwelt.

translation.en: He flew past the Isthmus, Mount Casius, and the vast Serbonian bog.
translation.kr: 그는 지협과 카시우스 산, 그리고 거대한 세르보니아 습지를 지나쳐 날아갔습니다.

translation.en: He traveled up the shore of Palestine, where the dark-faced Aethiops lived.
translation.kr: 그는 얼굴이 어두운 에티오피아 사람들이 사는 팔레스타인 해안을 따라 올라갔습니다.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: He flew on past pleasant hills and valleys, like Argos itself, or Lacedæmon, or the fair Vale of Tempe.  But the lowlands were all drowned by floods, and the highlands blasted by fire, and the hills heaved like a babbling cauldron, before the wrath of King Poseidon, the shaker of the earth.

translation.en: He flew past pleasant hills and valleys resembling his homeland of Argos.
translation.kr: 그는 고향 아르고스와 비슷한 쾌적한 언덕과 계곡들을 지났습니다.

translation.en: But the lowlands were all flooded, and the highlands were blasted by fire.
translation.kr: 하지만 저지대는 모두 홍수에 잠겼고, 고지대는 불에 타버렸습니다.

translation.en: The hills heaved like a boiling cauldron before the wrath of Poseidon.
translation.kr: 언덕들은 포세이돈의 분노 앞에서 끓어오르는 가마솥처럼 들썩였습니다.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: And Perseus feared to go inland, but flew along the shore above the sea; and he went on all the day, and the sky was black with smoke; and he went on all the night, and the sky was red with flame.

translation.en: Fearing to go inland, Perseus flew along the shore above the sea.
translation.kr: 내륙으로 들어가기를 두려워한 페르세우스는 바다 위 해안을 따라 날아갔습니다.

translation.en: He flew all day while the sky was black with smoke.
translation.kr: 그는 하늘이 연기로 검게 물든 온종일 날았습니다.

translation.en: He flew all night while the sky was red with flames.
translation.kr: 그는 하늘이 화염으로 붉게 물든 밤새도록 날았습니다.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: And at the dawn of day he looked toward the cliffs; and at the water’s edge, under a black rock, he saw a white image stand.

translation.en: At dawn, he looked toward the cliffs.
translation.kr: 새벽이 되자 그는 절벽 쪽을 바라보았습니다.

translation.en: At the water edge, beneath a black rock, he saw a white image standing.
translation.kr: 물가 가장자리, 검은 바위 아래에 하얀 형상이 서 있는 것을 보았습니다.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: ‘This,’ thought he, ‘must surely be the statue of some sea-God; I will go near and see what kind of Gods these barbarians worship.’

translation.en: He thought it must surely be the statue of some sea god.
translation.kr: 그는 그것이 틀림없이 어떤 바다 신의 조각상일 것이라고 생각했습니다.

translation.en: I will go near and see what kind of gods these barbarians worship, he decided.
translation.kr: 이 야만인들이 어떤 신을 숭배하는지 가까이 가서 보아야겠다, 그가 결심했습니다.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: So he came near; but when he came, it was no statue, but a maiden of flesh and blood; for he could see her tresses streaming in the breeze; and as he came closer still, he could see how she shrank and shivered when the waves sprinkled her with cold salt spray.  Her arms were spread above her head, and fastened to the rock with chains of brass; and her head drooped on her bosom, either with sleep, or weariness, or grief. But now and then she looked up and wailed, and called her mother; yet she did not see Perseus, for the cap of darkness was on his head.

translation.en: He approached and realized it was no statue, but a living maiden.
translation.kr: 그가 다가가 보니 그것은 조각상이 아니라 살아있는 처녀였습니다.

translation.en: Her tresses streamed in the breeze, and she shivered in the cold salt spray.
translation.kr: 그녀의 머리카락은 산들바람에 흩날렸고, 그녀는 차가운 바닷물보라를 맞으며 몸을 떨었습니다.

translation.en: Her arms were spread above her head and fastened to the rock with brass chains.
translation.kr: 그녀의 두 팔은 머리 위로 펼쳐진 채 놋쇠 사슬로 바위에 묶여 있었습니다.

translation.en: Her head drooped in exhaustion, sleep, or deep sorrow.
translation.kr: 그녀는 피로와 졸음, 혹은 깊은 슬픔으로 고개를 푹 숙이고 있었습니다.

translation.en: Occasionally she looked up and wailed for her mother.
translation.kr: 때때로 그녀는 고개를 들고 어머니를 부르며 울부짖었습니다.

translation.en: She did not see Perseus because he wore the cap of darkness.
translation.kr: 페르세우스는 어둠의 모자를 쓰고 있었기에 그녀는 그를 보지 못했습니다.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: [Picture: Perseus and the maid]

translation.en: [Picture: Perseus and the maid]
translation.kr: [그림: 페르세우스와 처녀]

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: Full of pity and indignation, Perseus drew near and looked upon the maid. Her cheeks were darker than his were, and her hair was blue-black like a hyacinth; but Perseus thought, ‘I have never seen so beautiful a maiden; no, not in all our isles.  Surely she is a king’s daughter.  Do barbarians treat their kings’ daughters thus?  She is too fair, at least, to have done any wrong I will speak to her.’

translation.en: Full of pity and anger, Perseus drew near to look upon the maid.
translation.kr: 연민과 분노로 가득 찬 페르세우스는 처녀를 바라보기 위해 다가갔습니다.

translation.en: Her cheeks were darker than his, and her hair was deep blue-black.
translation.kr: 그녀의 뺨은 그보다 어두웠고, 머리카락은 짙은 청흑색이었습니다.

translation.en: I have never seen so beautiful a maiden, he thought.
translation.kr: 이렇게 아름다운 처녀는 본 적이 없다, 그가 생각했습니다.

translation.en: Surely she is a king daughter.
translation.kr: 그녀는 틀림없이 왕의 딸일 것이다.

translation.en: Do barbarians treat their royal daughters like this?
translation.kr: 야만인들은 자신들의 공주를 이리도 대우한단 말인가?

translation.en: She is too fair to have done any wrong; I will speak to her.
translation.kr: 그녀는 죄를 짓기에는 너무도 아름답다; 내가 그녀에게 말을 걸어보리라.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: And, lifting the hat from his head, he flashed into her sight.  She shrieked with terror, and tried to hide her face with her hair, for she could not with her hands; but Perseus cried—

translation.en: Lifting the hat from his head, he flashed into her sight.
translation.kr: 그가 머리에서 모자를 벗자, 그녀의 시야에 그의 모습이 나타났습니다.

translation.en: She shrieked with terror and tried to hide her face with her hair.
translation.kr: 그녀는 공포에 질려 비명을 지르며 머리카락으로 얼굴을 가리려 했습니다.

translation.en: She could not use her bound hands, but Perseus cried out to her.
translation.kr: 손이 묶여 있어 손을 쓸 수 없는 그녀에게 페르세우스가 외쳤습니다.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: ‘Do not fear me, fair one; I am a Hellen, and no barbarian.  What cruel men have bound you?  But first I will set you free.’

translation.en: Do not fear me, fair one; I am a Greek, not a barbarian.
translation.kr: 두려워하지 마십시오, 아름다운 분; 저는 야만인이 아니라 그리스인입니다.

translation.en: What cruel men have bound you?
translation.kr: 어떤 잔인한 자들이 당신을 묶었습니까?

translation.en: First, I will set you free.
translation.kr: 먼저 제가 당신을 풀어드리겠습니다.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: And he tore at the fetters, but they were too strong for him; while the maiden cried—

translation.en: He tore at the fetters, but they were too strong for him.
translation.kr: 그는 족쇄를 뜯어내려 했지만 그에게도 너무 단단했습니다.

translation.en: The maiden cried out to him in distress.
translation.kr: 처녀가 괴로워하며 그에게 외쳤습니다.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: ‘Touch me not; I am accursed, devoted as a victim to the sea-Gods.  They will slay you, if you dare to set me free.’

translation.en: Do not touch me; I am cursed, chosen as a victim for the sea gods.
translation.kr: 제게 손대지 마세요; 저는 저주를 받아 바다 신들의 제물로 바쳐졌습니다.

translation.en: They will kill you if you dare to set me free.
translation.kr: 당신이 저를 풀어주려 한다면 그들이 당신을 죽일 것입니다.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: ‘Let them try,’ said Perseus; and drawing, Herpé from his thigh, he cut through the brass as if it had been flax.

translation.en: Let them try, Perseus said.
translation.kr: 어디 한번 해보라지요, 페르세우스가 말했습니다.

translation.en: Drawing his sword from his side, he cut through the brass like flax.
translation.kr: 그는 허리에서 검을 뽑아 놋쇠를 실타래처럼 베어버렸습니다.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: ‘Now,’ he said, ‘you belong to me, and not to these sea-Gods, whosoever they may be!’  But she only called the more on her mother.

translation.en: Now you belong to me, not to these sea gods, whoever they are!
translation.kr: 이제 당신은 그 바다 신들이 누구든 그들이 아니라 저에게 속해 있습니다!

translation.en: But she only called out for her mother all the more.
translation.kr: 하지만 그녀는 오직 어머니만을 더욱 애타게 불렀습니다.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: ‘Why call on your mother?  She can be no mother to have left you here. If a bird is dropped out of the nest, it belongs to the man who picks it up.  If a jewel is cast by the wayside, it is his who dare win it and wear it, as I will win you and will wear you.  I know now why Pallas Athené sent me hither.  She sent me to gain a prize worth all my toil and more.’

translation.en: Why call for your mother?
translation.kr: 어찌하여 어머니를 부르십니까?

translation.en: She cannot be a true mother to have left you here.
translation.kr: 당신을 이곳에 버려둔 분이 진정한 어머니일 리 없습니다.

translation.en: If a bird drops from the nest, it belongs to the man who picks it up.
translation.kr: 둥지에서 떨어진 새는 그 새를 줍는 사람의 것입니다.

translation.en: I will win you and cherish you.
translation.kr: 제가 당신을 얻고 당신을 소중히 여길 것입니다.

translation.en: I now know why Athena sent me here.
translation.kr: 아테나 여신께서 왜 저를 이곳에 보내셨는지 이제 알겠습니다.

translation.en: She sent me to gain a prize worth all my toil.
translation.kr: 제 모든 고생을 보상하고도 남을 귀한 분을 얻게 하시려 저를 보내신 것입니다.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: And he clasped her in his arms, and cried, ‘Where are these sea-Gods, cruel and unjust, who doom fair maids to death?  I carry the weapons of Immortals.  Let them measure their strength against mine!  But tell me, maiden, who you are, and what dark fate brought you here.’

translation.en: He clasped her in his arms and cried out to the heavens.
translation.kr: 그는 그녀를 품에 안고 하늘을 향해 외쳤습니다.

translation.en: Where are these cruel gods who doom fair maids to death?
translation.kr: 아름다운 처녀를 죽음으로 내모는 잔인한 신들은 어디에 있는가?

translation.en: I carry the weapons of immortals; let them fight me!
translation.kr: 나는 불멸의 신들의 무기를 지니고 있다; 나와 맞서 싸워보라!

translation.en: Tell me, maiden, who are you and what dark fate brought you here?
translation.kr: 말씀해 보십시오, 당신은 누구시며 어떤 어두운 운명이 당신을 이곳으로 이끌었습니까?

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: And she answered, weeping—

translation.en: And she answered, weeping:
translation.kr: 그러자 그녀가 울면서 대답했습니다.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: ‘I am the daughter of Cepheus, King of Iopa, and my mother is Cassiopoeia of the beautiful tresses, and they called me Andromeda, as long as life was mine.  And I stand bound here, hapless that I am, for the sea-monster’s food, to atone for my mother’s sin.  For she boasted of me once that I was fairer than Atergatis, Queen of the Fishes; so she in her wrath sent the sea-floods, and her brother the Fire King sent the earthquakes, and wasted all the land, and after the floods a monster bred of the slime, who devours all living things.  And now he must devour me, guiltless though I am—me who never harmed a living thing, nor saw a fish upon the shore but I gave it life, and threw it back into the sea; for in our land we eat no fish, for fear of Atergatis their queen.  Yet the priests say that nothing but my blood can atone for a sin which I never committed.’

translation.en: I am Andromeda, daughter of King Cepheus and Queen Cassiopeia.
translation.kr: 저는 케페우스 왕과 카시오페이아 왕비의 딸인 안드로메다입니다.

translation.en: I am bound here as food for the sea monster to pay for my mother sin.
translation.kr: 저는 어머니의 죄를 씻기 위해 바다 괴물의 먹이로 이곳에 묶여 있습니다.

translation.en: She once boasted that I was fairer than the Queen of the Fishes.
translation.kr: 어머니는 한때 제가 물고기들의 여왕보다 더 아름답다고 자랑하셨습니다.

translation.en: In wrath, the queen sent floods, and her brother sent earthquakes.
translation.kr: 분노한 여왕은 홍수를 보냈고, 그녀의 오빠는 지진을 일으켜 온 땅을 황폐하게 했습니다.

translation.en: After the floods came a monster bred of slime, devouring all living things.
translation.kr: 홍수가 끝난 후 진흙에서 태어난 괴물이 나타나 살아있는 모든 것을 집어삼켰습니다.

translation.en: Now it must devour me, though I am entirely guiltless.
translation.kr: 저는 아무런 죄가 없건만, 이제 그 괴물이 저를 먹어 치울 것입니다.

translation.en: I never harmed a living thing in my life.
translation.kr: 저는 평생 살아있는 그 어떤 것도 해친 적이 없습니다.

translation.en: If I found a fish on the shore, I safely returned it to the sea.
translation.kr: 해변에서 물고기를 발견하면 언제나 안전하게 바다로 돌려보냈습니다.

translation.en: Yet the priests say only my blood can atone for a sin I did not commit.
translation.kr: 그럼에도 제사장들은 제가 짓지도 않은 죄를 씻을 방법은 제 피뿐이라고 말합니다.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: But Perseus laughed, and said, ‘A sea-monster?  I have fought with worse than him: I would have faced Immortals for your sake; how much more a beast of the sea?’

translation.en: Perseus laughed and said, A sea monster?
translation.kr: 페르세우스가 웃으며 말했습니다. 바다 괴물이라고요?

translation.en: I have fought with worse than him.
translation.kr: 저는 그보다 훨씬 끔찍한 존재와도 싸웠습니다.

translation.en: I would face immortals for your sake; how much more a simple sea beast?
translation.kr: 당신을 위해서라면 불멸의 신들과도 맞설 텐데, 일개 바다 짐승쯤이야 문제겠습니까?

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: Then Andromeda looked up at him, and new hope was kindled in her breast, so proud and fair did he stand, with one hand round her, and in the other the glittering sword.  But she only sighed, and wept the more, and cried—

translation.en: Andromeda looked up at him, and new hope kindled in her heart.
translation.kr: 안드로메다가 그를 올려다보자 그녀의 마음에 새로운 희망이 피어올랐습니다.

translation.en: He stood so proud and fair, holding her and his glittering sword.
translation.kr: 그는 한 팔로 그녀를 안고 다른 손에는 빛나는 검을 든 채 늠름하게 서 있었습니다.

translation.en: But she sighed, wept even more, and cried out to him.
translation.kr: 하지만 그녀는 한숨을 쉬고 더 많은 눈물을 흘리며 외쳤습니다.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: ‘Why will you die, young as you are?  Is there not death and sorrow enough in the world already?  It is noble for me to die, that I may save the lives of a whole people; but you, better than them all, why should I slay you too?  Go you your way; I must go mine.’

translation.en: Why should you die when you are so young?
translation.kr: 당신처럼 젊은 분이 왜 목숨을 버리려 하십니까?

translation.en: Is there not enough death and sorrow in the world already?
translation.kr: 세상에는 이미 죽음과 슬픔이 충분하지 않은가요?

translation.en: It is noble for me to die to save a whole people.
translation.kr: 모든 백성을 구하기 위해 제가 죽는 것은 고귀한 일입니다.

translation.en: But why should I cause your death as well?
translation.kr: 하지만 당신까지 죽게 내버려 둘 수는 없습니다.

translation.en: Go your way, and I must go mine.
translation.kr: 당신은 당신의 길을 가십시오. 저는 제 길을 가야 합니다.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: But Perseus cried, ‘Not so; for the Lords of Olympus, whom I serve, are the friends of the heroes, and help them on to noble deeds.  Led by them, I slew the Gorgon, the beautiful horror; and not without them do I come hither, to slay this monster with that same Gorgon’s head.  Yet hide your eyes when I leave you, lest the sight of it freeze you too to stone.’

translation.en: Not so, for the gods I serve are friends of heroes.
translation.kr: 그렇지 않습니다. 제가 모시는 신들은 영웅들의 편이십니다.

translation.en: Led by them, I slew the Gorgon, that beautiful horror.
translation.kr: 저는 그분들의 인도로 그 아름답고 끔찍한 고르곤을 죽였습니다.

translation.en: They guided me here to slay this monster with the Gorgon head.
translation.kr: 그분들께서 고르곤의 머리로 이 괴물을 처치하라고 저를 이곳으로 이끄셨습니다.

translation.en: When I leave you, hide your eyes so the head does not turn you to stone.
translation.kr: 제가 당신 곁을 떠날 때, 돌로 변하지 않도록 눈을 가리십시오.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: But the maiden answered nothing, for she could not believe his words. And then, suddenly looking up, she pointed to the sea, and shrieked—

translation.en: The maiden could not believe his words and remained silent.
translation.kr: 처녀는 그의 말을 믿을 수 없어 아무 대답도 하지 못했습니다.

translation.en: Suddenly looking up, she pointed to the sea and shrieked.
translation.kr: 갑자기 고개를 든 그녀가 바다를 가리키며 비명을 질렀습니다.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: ‘There he comes, with the sunrise, as they promised.  I must die now. How shall I endure it?  Oh, go!  Is it not dreadful enough to be torn piecemeal, without having you to look on?’  And she tried to thrust him away.

translation.en: He comes with the sunrise, exactly as they promised.
translation.kr: 그들이 말한 대로 괴물이 일출과 함께 오고 있습니다.

translation.en: I must die now; how shall I endure it?
translation.kr: 저는 이제 죽어야만 합니다. 이 고통을 어찌 견딜까요?

translation.en: Oh, please go! It is dreadful enough to be torn to pieces.
translation.kr: 오, 제발 가세요! 갈가리 찢기는 것만으로도 충분히 끔찍합니다.

translation.en: I cannot bear to watch you die as well.
translation.kr: 당신마저 죽는 모습을 차마 볼 수 없습니다.

translation.en: She tried desperately to thrust him away.
translation.kr: 그녀는 필사적으로 그를 밀어내려 했습니다.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: But he said, ‘I go; yet promise me one thing ere I go: that if I slay this beast you will be my wife, and come back with me to my kingdom in fruitful Argos, for I am a king’s heir.  Promise me, and seal it with a kiss.’

translation.en: I will go, but promise me one thing before I fight.
translation.kr: 물러나겠습니다. 하지만 싸우기 전에 한 가지 약속을 해주십시오.

translation.en: If I slay this beast, you will become my wife.
translation.kr: 제가 이 괴물을 물리친다면 당신은 저의 아내가 되어주셔야 합니다.

translation.en: You must come back with me to my kingdom in Argos, for I am a king heir.
translation.kr: 저는 왕의 후계자이니, 저와 함께 아르고스에 있는 제 왕국으로 가야 합니다.

translation.en: Promise me, and seal it with a kiss.
translation.kr: 저에게 약속하고 입맞춤으로 그 징표를 삼아 주십시오.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: Then she lifted up her face, and kissed him; and Perseus laughed for joy, and flew upward, while Andromeda crouched trembling on the rock, waiting for what might befall.

translation.en: She lifted her face and kissed him.
translation.kr: 그녀가 고개를 들어 그에게 입을 맞추었습니다.

translation.en: Perseus laughed for joy and flew upward into the air.
translation.kr: 페르세우스는 기뻐 웃으며 하늘 위로 날아올랐습니다.

translation.en: Andromeda crouched trembling on the rock, waiting for what would happen.
translation.kr: 안드로메다는 바위 위에서 몸을 웅크리고 떨며 다가올 일들을 기다렸습니다.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: On came the great sea-monster, coasting along like a huge black galley, lazily breasting the ripple, and stopping at times by creek or headland to watch for the laughter of girls at their bleaching, or cattle pawing on the sand-hills, or boys bathing on the beach.  His great sides were fringed with clustering shells and sea-weeds, and the water gurgled in and out of his wide jaws, as he rolled along, dripping and glistening in the beams of the morning sun.

translation.en: The great sea monster cruised forward like a huge black galley.
translation.kr: 거대한 바다 괴물은 거대한 검은 갤리선처럼 바다를 가르며 다가왔습니다.

translation.en: It paused by creeks and headlands, searching for prey.
translation.kr: 괴물은 작은 만과 곶에서 먹잇감을 찾으며 멈춰 섰습니다.

translation.en: Its sides were fringed with clustering shells and seaweed.
translation.kr: 그의 옆구리에는 조개껍데기와 해초가 잔뜩 붙어 있었습니다.

translation.en: Water gurgled in its wide jaws as it rolled along the waves.
translation.kr: 물결을 따라 구를 때마다 쩍 벌어진 턱에서 물소리가 났습니다.

translation.en: Its dark scales glistened in the morning sun.
translation.kr: 녀석의 어두운 비늘은 아침 햇살을 받아 번쩍였습니다.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: At last he saw Andromeda, and shot forward to take his prey, while the waves foamed white behind him, and before him the fish fled leaping.

translation.en: At last, it spotted Andromeda and shot forward to take its prey.
translation.kr: 마침내 안드로메다를 발견한 녀석은 먹잇감을 향해 빠르게 돌진했습니다.

translation.en: Waves foamed white behind it while terrified fish fled leaping before it.
translation.kr: 녀석의 뒤로는 하얀 파도가 일었고, 앞에서는 공포에 질린 물고기들이 뛰어오르며 도망쳤습니다.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: Then down from the height of the air fell Perseus like a shooting star; down to the crests of the waves, while Andromeda hid her face as he shouted; and then there was silence for a while.

translation.en: Then Perseus plummeted from the sky like a shooting star.
translation.kr: 그때 페르세우스가 별똥별처럼 하늘에서 떨어져 내렸습니다.

translation.en: He descended to the crests of the waves with a mighty shout.
translation.kr: 그는 큰 함성과 함께 파도 꼭대기로 내려왔습니다.

translation.en: Andromeda hid her face, and then a heavy silence fell.
translation.kr: 안드로메다가 얼굴을 가리자, 깊은 침묵이 찾아왔습니다.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: At last she looked up trembling, and saw Perseus springing toward her; and instead of the monster a long black rock, with the sea rippling quietly round it.

translation.en: Trembling, she finally looked up and saw Perseus springing toward her.
translation.kr: 떨며 마침내 고개를 든 그녀는 페르세우스가 자신에게 달려오는 것을 보았습니다.

translation.en: Instead of the monster, there was a long black rock with quiet ripples around it.
translation.kr: 괴물 대신 길고 검은 바위 하나만이 잔잔한 물결 속에 남아 있었습니다.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: Who then so proud as Perseus, as he leapt back to the rock, and lifted his fair Andromeda in his arms, and flew with her to the cliff-top, as a falcon carries a dove?

translation.en: Perseus leapt back to the rock with immense pride.
translation.kr: 페르세우스는 벅찬 자부심을 안고 바위로 뛰어올랐습니다.

translation.en: He lifted his fair Andromeda in his arms and flew to the cliff top.
translation.kr: 그는 아름다운 안드로메다를 안고 독수리가 비둘기를 안듯 절벽 위로 날아올랐습니다.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: Who so proud as Perseus, and who so joyful as all the Æthiop people?  For they had stood watching the monster from the cliffs, wailing for the maiden’s fate.  And already a messenger had gone to Cepheus and Cassiopoeia, where they sat in sackcloth and ashes on the ground, in the innermost palace chambers, awaiting their daughter’s end.  And they came, and all the city with them, to see the wonder, with songs and with dances, with cymbals and harps, and received their daughter back again, as one alive from the dead.

translation.en: Perseus was incredibly proud, and the Aethiopian people were overjoyed.
translation.kr: 페르세우스는 매우 자랑스러웠고, 에티오피아 백성들은 뛸 듯이 기뻐했습니다.

translation.en: They had watched the monster from the cliffs, mourning the maiden fate.
translation.kr: 그들은 절벽 위에서 괴물을 지켜보며 처녀의 운명을 슬퍼하고 있었습니다.

translation.en: A messenger had already rushed to King Cepheus and Queen Cassiopeia.
translation.kr: 전령이 이미 케페우스 왕과 카시오페이아 왕비에게 달려간 후였습니다.

translation.en: The royal couple sat in ashes in the palace, awaiting their daughter end.
translation.kr: 왕과 왕비는 궁전 깊은 곳에서 재를 뒤집어쓴 채 딸의 최후를 기다리고 있었습니다.

translation.en: They came with the whole city to witness the miracle.
translation.kr: 그들은 기적을 보기 위해 온 도시 사람들과 함께 달려왔습니다.

translation.en: With songs, dances, and harps, they received their daughter back from the dead.
translation.kr: 그들은 노래와 춤, 수금 연주와 함께 죽음에서 살아 돌아온 딸을 맞이했습니다.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: Then Cepheus said, ‘Hero of the Hellens, stay here with me and be my son-in-law, and I will give you the half of my kingdom.’

translation.en: Cepheus said, Hero of the Greeks, stay and be my son-in-law.
translation.kr: 케페우스가 말했습니다. 그리스의 영웅이여, 이곳에 머물며 제 사위가 되어 주십시오.

translation.en: I will give you half of my kingdom.
translation.kr: 제 왕국의 절반을 드리겠습니다.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: ‘I will be your son-in-law,’ said Perseus, ‘but of your kingdom I will have none, for I long after the pleasant land of Greece, and my mother who waits for me at home.’

translation.en: I will be your son-in-law, Perseus replied.
translation.kr: 제가 기꺼이 사위가 되겠습니다, 페르세우스가 대답했습니다.

translation.en: But I will take none of your kingdom.
translation.kr: 하지만 왕국은 한 치도 받지 않겠습니다.

translation.en: I long for the pleasant land of Greece and my mother who waits for me.
translation.kr: 저는 아름다운 그리스 땅과 저를 기다리는 어머니가 몹시 그립습니다.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: Then Cepheus said, ‘You must not take my daughter away at once, for she is to us like one alive from the dead.  Stay with us here a year, and after that you shall return with honour.’  And Perseus consented; but before he went to the palace he bade the people bring stones and wood, and built three altars, one to Athené, and one to Hermes, and one to Father Zeus, and offered bullocks and rams.

translation.en: You must not take my daughter away immediately, Cepheus said.
translation.kr: 내 딸을 당장 데려가서는 안 되네, 케페우스가 말했습니다.

translation.en: She is like someone returned from the dead to us.
translation.kr: 그녀는 우리에게 죽음에서 살아 돌아온 사람과 같네.

translation.en: Stay with us for a year, and then return with great honor.
translation.kr: 우리와 함께 일 년을 머물고, 그 후에 큰 명예를 안고 돌아가게.

translation.en: Perseus consented and asked the people to bring stones and wood.
translation.kr: 페르세우스는 승낙했고, 사람들에게 돌과 나무를 가져오라고 지시했습니다.

translation.en: He built three altars to Athena, Hermes, and Zeus, and offered sacrifices.
translation.kr: 그는 아테나, 헤르메스, 제우스를 위해 세 개의 제단을 쌓고 제물을 바쳤습니다.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: And some said, ‘This is a pious man;’ yet the priests said, ‘The Sea Queen will be yet more fierce against us, because her monster is slain.’ But they were afraid to speak aloud, for they feared the Gorgon’s head. So they went up to the palace; and when they came in, there stood in the hall Phineus, the brother of Cepheus, chafing like a bear robbed of her whelps, and with him his sons, and his servants, and many an armed man; and he cried to Cepheus—

translation.en: Many declared him a pious man.
translation.kr: 많은 이들이 그를 경건한 사람이라 칭송했습니다.

translation.en: Yet the priests muttered that the Sea Queen would become even more furious.
translation.kr: 하지만 제사장들은 바다의 여왕이 괴물의 죽음으로 더욱 분노할 것이라 투덜거렸습니다.

translation.en: They were afraid to speak aloud because they feared the Gorgon head.
translation.kr: 그들은 고르곤의 머리가 두려워 감히 소리 내어 말하지 못했습니다.

translation.en: When they reached the palace hall, Phineus, the king brother, stood waiting.
translation.kr: 그들이 궁전 회랑에 이르자, 왕의 동생 피네우스가 기다리고 있었습니다.

translation.en: He was furious, pacing like a bear robbed of her cubs.
translation.kr: 그는 새끼를 빼앗긴 곰처럼 격노하여 서성거리고 있었습니다.

translation.en: With him were his sons, servants, and many armed men.
translation.kr: 그의 곁에는 아들들과 하인들, 수많은 무장 병력들이 함께 있었습니다.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: ‘You shall not marry your daughter to this stranger, of whom no one knows even the name.  Was not Andromeda betrothed to my son?  And now she is safe again, has he not a right to claim her?’

translation.en: You shall not marry your daughter to this nameless stranger, he yelled.
translation.kr: 당신의 딸을 이름도 모르는 이방인과 결혼시킬 수는 없습니다, 그가 소리쳤습니다.

translation.en: Was Andromeda not betrothed to my son?
translation.kr: 안드로메다는 내 아들과 약혼한 사이가 아닙니까?

translation.en: Now that she is safe, does he not have the right to claim her?
translation.kr: 이제 그녀가 무사히 돌아왔으니, 내 아들이 그녀를 차지할 권리가 있지 않습니까?

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: But Perseus laughed, and answered, ‘If your son is in want of a bride, let him save a maiden for himself.  As yet he seems but a helpless bride-groom.  He left this one to die, and dead she is to him.  I saved her alive, and alive she is to me, but to no one else.  Ungrateful man! have I not saved your land, and the lives of your sons and daughters, and will you requite me thus?  Go, or it will be worse for you.’  But all the men-at-arms drew their swords, and rushed on him like wild beasts.

translation.en: Perseus laughed and answered the angry man.
translation.kr: 페르세우스가 웃으며 분노한 남자에게 대답했습니다.

translation.en: If your son wants a bride, let him save a maiden for himself.
translation.kr: 당신의 아들이 신부를 원한다면 직접 나서서 처녀를 구하라고 하십시오.

translation.en: He seems but a helpless bridegroom who left this one to die.
translation.kr: 그는 신부를 죽게 내버려 둔 무능한 자에 불과합니다.

translation.en: She is dead to him, but she is alive to me because I saved her.
translation.kr: 그에게 그녀는 죽은 사람이지만, 제가 구했기에 저에게는 살아있는 사람입니다.

translation.en: Ungrateful man, have I not saved your land and your children?
translation.kr: 은혜를 모르는 자여, 내가 당신의 땅과 당신의 자식들을 구하지 않았습니까?

translation.en: Leave now, or it will be worse for you.
translation.kr: 지금 떠나지 않으면 끔찍한 대가를 치를 것입니다.

translation.en: But the armed men drew their swords and rushed at him like wild beasts.
translation.kr: 하지만 무장한 남자들은 검을 뽑아 들고 짐승처럼 그에게 달려들었습니다.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: Then he unveiled the Gorgon’s head, and said, ‘This has delivered my bride from one wild beast: it shall deliver her from many.’  And as he spoke Phineus and all his men-at-arms stopped short, and stiffened each man as he stood; and before Perseus had drawn the goat-skin over the face again, they were all turned into stone.

translation.en: He unveiled the Gorgon head.
translation.kr: 그는 고르곤의 머리를 꺼내 들었습니다.

translation.en: This delivered my bride from one beast; it shall deliver her from many.
translation.kr: 이것이 야수 하나로부터 내 신부를 구했으니, 이제 수많은 야수들로부터도 그녀를 구할 것이다.

translation.en: As he spoke, Phineus and all his men stopped short and stiffened.
translation.kr: 그가 말하는 순간 피네우스와 그의 부하들은 그 자리에 멈춰 서서 굳어버렸습니다.

translation.en: Before Perseus covered the face again, they had all turned to stone.
translation.kr: 페르세우스가 다시 염소 가죽으로 그 얼굴을 덮기도 전에, 그들은 모두 돌로 변했습니다.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: Then Perseuss bade the people bring levers and roll them out; and what was done with them after that I cannot tell.

translation.en: Perseus commanded the people to bring levers and roll the statues out.
translation.kr: 페르세우스는 사람들에게 지렛대를 가져와 조각상들을 밖으로 굴려 내라고 명령했습니다.

translation.en: What was done with them after that, I cannot tell.
translation.kr: 그 후 그 조각상들이 어찌 되었는지는 알 수 없습니다.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: So they made a great wedding-feast, which lasted seven whole days, and who so happy as Perseus and Andromeda?

translation.en: They held a grand wedding feast that lasted seven entire days.
translation.kr: 그들은 칠 일 밤낮으로 성대한 결혼 잔치를 열었습니다.

translation.en: No one was as happy as Perseus and Andromeda.
translation.kr: 페르세우스와 안드로메다만큼 행복한 사람은 없었습니다.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: But on the eighth night Perseus dreamed a dream; and he saw standing beside him Pallas Athené, as he had seen her in Seriphos, seven long years before; and she stood and called him by name, and said—

translation.en: On the eighth night, Perseus dreamed a remarkable dream.
translation.kr: 여덟째 날 밤, 페르세우스는 놀라운 꿈을 꾸었습니다.

translation.en: Athena stood beside him, just as she had in Seriphos seven years before.
translation.kr: 칠 년 전 세리포스에서 그랬듯, 아테나 여신이 그의 곁에 서 있었습니다.

translation.en: She called him by name and spoke to him gently.
translation.kr: 그녀는 그의 이름을 부르며 부드럽게 말했습니다.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: ‘Perseus, you have played the man, and see, you have your reward.  Know now that the Gods are just, and help him who helps himself.  Now give me here Herpé the sword, and the sandals, and the hat of darkness, that I may give them back to their owners; but the Gorgon’s head you shall keep a while, for you will need it in your land of Greece.  Then you shall lay it up in my temple at Seriphos, that I may wear it on my shield for ever, a terror to the Titans and the monsters, and the foes of Gods and men. And as for this land, I have appeased the sea and the fire, and there shall be no more floods nor earthquakes.  But let the people build altars to Father Zeus, and to me, and worship the Immortals, the Lords of heaven and earth.’

translation.en: Perseus, you have proved yourself a true man, and here is your reward.
translation.kr: 페르세우스야, 너는 진정한 영웅임을 증명했고, 여기 네 보상이 있다.

translation.en: Know that the gods are just and help those who help themselves.
translation.kr: 신들은 공정하며 스스로 돕는 자를 돕는다는 것을 명심하여라.

translation.en: Return to me the sword, sandals, and hat of darkness to give back to their owners.
translation.kr: 검과 샌들, 어둠의 모자는 원래 주인들에게 돌려주어야 하니 내게 다오.

translation.en: You may keep the Gorgon head for a while, as you will need it in Greece.
translation.kr: 고르곤의 머리는 그리스에서 필요할 테니 당분간 네가 간직하여라.

translation.en: Afterward, place it in my temple at Seriphos.
translation.kr: 그 후에 세리포스에 있는 내 신전에 그것을 바쳐라.

translation.en: I will wear it on my shield forever as a terror to monsters.
translation.kr: 내가 그것을 내 방패에 영원히 새겨 괴물들에게 공포를 심어주마.

translation.en: I have appeased the sea and fire in this land.
translation.kr: 나는 이 땅의 바다와 불의 분노를 잠재웠다.

translation.en: Let the people worship the immortals and fear floods no more.
translation.kr: 백성들이 불멸의 신들을 숭배하고 다시는 홍수를 두려워하지 않게 하여라.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: And Perseus rose to give her the sword, and the cap, and the sandals; but he woke, and his dream vanished away.  And yet it was not altogether a dream; for the goat-skin with the head was in its place; but the sword, and the cap, and the sandals were gone, and Perseus never saw them more.

translation.en: Perseus rose to give her the items, but he woke and the dream vanished.
translation.kr: 페르세우스가 물건을 주려고 일어났을 때 잠에서 깼고 꿈은 사라졌습니다.

translation.en: Yet it was not merely a dream.
translation.kr: 하지만 그것은 단순한 꿈이 아니었습니다.

translation.en: The goatskin with the head remained, but the sword, cap, and sandals were gone.
translation.kr: 머리가 든 가죽 주머니는 그대로 있었지만, 검과 모자, 샌들은 사라졌습니다.

translation.en: Perseus never saw them again.
translation.kr: 페르세우스는 그것들을 다시는 볼 수 없었습니다.

part: Part IV: How Perseus Came to the Æthiops
raw: Then a great awe fell on Perseus; and he went out in the morning to the people, and told his dream, and bade them build altars to Zeus, the Father of Gods and men, and to Athené, who gives wisdom to heroes; and fear no more the earthquakes and the floods, but sow and build in peace. And they did so for a while, and prospered; but after Perseus was gone they forgot Zeus and Athené, and worshipped again Atergatis the queen, and the undying fish of the sacred lake, where Deucalion’s deluge was swallowed up, and they burnt their children before the Fire King, till Zeus was angry with that foolish people, and brought a strange nation against them out of Egypt, who fought against them and wasted them utterly, and dwelt in their cities for many a hundred years.

translation.en: A great awe fell upon Perseus.
translation.kr: 페르세우스는 깊은 경외감에 사로잡혔습니다.

translation.en: In the morning, he told the people his dream.
translation.kr: 아침이 되자 그는 백성들에게 자신의 꿈을 이야기했습니다.

translation.en: He asked them to build altars to Zeus and Athena and live in peace.
translation.kr: 그는 제우스와 아테나에게 제단을 쌓고 평화롭게 살라고 당부했습니다.

translation.en: They did so and prospered for a while.
translation.kr: 그들은 말씀대로 행했고 한동안 번영을 누렸습니다.

translation.en: But after Perseus left, they forgot the gods and worshipped the fish queen again.
translation.kr: 하지만 페르세우스가 떠난 후, 그들은 신들을 잊고 다시 물고기 여왕을 숭배했습니다.

translation.en: They sacrificed their children to the Fire King until Zeus grew angry.
translation.kr: 그들이 불의 왕에게 아이들을 제물로 바치자 제우스가 크게 분노했습니다.

translation.en: Zeus brought a strange nation from Egypt to destroy them.
translation.kr: 제우스는 이집트에서 이방 민족을 데려와 그들을 파멸시켰습니다.

translation.en: These invaders wasted the foolish people and ruled their cities for centuries.
translation.kr: 이 침략자들은 어리석은 백성들을 짓밟고 수백 년 동안 그들의 도시를 지배했습니다.
